## Week 1 — Value, GC, and entry {#week-01}

Full notes: [Week 1](week-01.qmd) · On-week Self-check: [Week 1 · Self-check](week-01.qmd#self-check) · 5 questions.

```{=html}
<div class="selfcheck" id="selfcheck-w01" data-week="01">
  <p class="selfcheck-intro">Five questions from Week 1 learning objectives, the Study checklist, and named formulas only. Keep the standing guards: <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>; OHKF <strong>HK$350bn</strong> = industry <em>value added</em>; ~1,000&nbsp;m ≠ Cap.&nbsp;448G flying limit; <strong>U-space ≠ Hong Kong law</strong>.</p>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w01-q1" data-correct="b">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">1. In these notes, the low-altitude economy (LAE) is best defined as…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q1" value="a"> Only passenger eVTOL “flying cars.”</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q1" value="b"> Economic activity that uses low-altitude airspace together with aircraft, sites, digital systems, operators, customers, and supporting services — a whole mission system, not an airframe alone.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q1" value="c"> The Cap. 448G statute itself.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q1" value="d"> A synonym for U-space under Hong Kong law.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>LAE is framed as a <strong>mission / service system</strong> (Learning objective 1; Study checklist 1; §1). “Flying cars only” misses logistics, inspection, EMS, and supporting services. Cap. 448G is Hong Kong’s SUA frame, not the definition of LAE. U-space is an EU / industry frame — <strong>not</strong> Hong Kong law.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w01-q2" data-correct="c">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">2. Hong Kong policy language often describes LAE as activity generally below about 1,000&nbsp;m. That figure is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q2" value="a"> The Cap. 448G Category A2 flying ceiling for ordinary SUA operations.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q2" value="b"> Permission to fly any SUA to 1,000&nbsp;m AGL without further CAD approval.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q2" value="c"> A policy / economic working description of the LAE field — <em>not</em> a Cap. 448G ordinary flying-height limit (those bands are 100&nbsp;ft / 300&nbsp;ft AGL unless CAD grants permission).</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q2" value="d"> The same thing as Mainland 120&nbsp;m / 300&nbsp;m (真高) labels under 国令761.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Keep the layers separate (Study checklist 2; §1 Policy band vs flying limits). ~1,000&nbsp;m is policy framing of the economic field. Cap. 448G ordinary bands are <strong>100&nbsp;ft</strong> (A1) and <strong>300&nbsp;ft ≈ 91&nbsp;m</strong> (A2) AGL. Mainland height labels are a different scheme.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w01-q3" data-correct="a">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">3. When these notes quote “about HK$350 billion,” the correct attribution is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q3" value="a"> Our Hong Kong Foundation (OHKF) scenario projection for Hong Kong LAE industry <em>value added</em> by 2050 — a private think-tank figure, not an HKSAR government target, not operator revenue, and not automatic GDP.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q3" value="b"> An HKSAR Policy Address binding spending commitment for 2030.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q3" value="c"> Total operator ticket revenue across all Hong Kong LAE firms today.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q3" value="d"> A Mainland 规模 (scale) total that already includes Hong Kong GDP.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Attribution rule (§5; Study checklist 11): name <strong>OHKF</strong>, metric (<strong>industry value added</strong>), geography (<strong>Hong Kong</strong>), horizon (<strong>2050</strong>). Value added ≠ revenue. Not a government target; not Mainland scale totals.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w01-q4" data-correct="d">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">4. Which statement about Hong Kong sandboxes is correct?</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q4" value="a"> The first Regulatory Sandbox and Sandbox X are the same programme under two names.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q4" value="b"> Entering a sandbox waives Cap. 448G and airworthiness duties for commercial flights.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q4" value="c"> First-batch selection “38 of 72” is the same statistic as Sandbox X’s “33 modules” total.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q4" value="d"> Sandboxes support controlled testing and can reduce learning cost, delay, and uncertainty in the entry-barrier sum — they do <em>not</em> waive safety or compliance; keep the first Regulatory Sandbox (e.g. 38 of 72) separate from Sandbox X (e.g. 33 modules).</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 5; Study checklist 8–9; §§10–11. <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>. A sandbox changes economic entry frictions; it is not a safety waiver. Cite first-batch and Sandbox X counts separately (<a href="key-figures.qmd">Key figures</a>).</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w01-q5" data-correct="b">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">5. Generalized cost (short form) in Week 1 is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q5" value="a"> Ticket price only — time does not enter mode choice.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q5" value="b"> GC = ticket price + VOT × travel time — money and time in one comparable burden; a maximum fare against an alternative follows from matching that GC.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q5" value="c"> The same identity as U-space charges under Hong Kong statute.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w01-q5" value="d"> NPV of the initial investment alone, with no operating cash flows.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Named formula on <a href="formulas.qmd#w01-gc">Formulas · Week 1 · GC</a> and §7. GC puts money and time on one scale; <em>P</em><sub>max</sub> follows from matching an alternative’s GC (§8 AE ceiling illustration). U-space is <strong>not</strong> Hong Kong law; NPV is a separate viability screen (− initial investment + present value of future profits).</div>
  </fieldset>
</div>
```

## Week 2 — Competition, cost, and co-opetition {#week-02}

Full notes: [Week 2](week-02.qmd) · On-week Self-check: [Week 2 · Self-check](week-02.qmd#self-check) · 4 questions.

```{=html}
<div class="selfcheck" id="selfcheck-w02" data-week="02">
  <p class="selfcheck-intro">Four questions from Week 2 learning objectives, the Study checklist, and named formulas (HHI, ATC, density, Bertrand / co-opetition). Keep <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>; corridor policy / trial ≠ day-to-day operating service.</p>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w02-q1" data-correct="d">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">1. Before talking about “competition in LAE,” these notes first ask you to…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q1" value="a"> Treat all LAE services as one city-wide market with a single HHI.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q1" value="b"> Use Sandbox X module counts as market shares.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q1" value="c"> Assume Bertrand P = MC always holds when pads are scarce.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q1" value="d"> Define a <em>narrow</em> market (product + geography + customer + layer) — LAE is not one market structure.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 1; Study checklist 1–2; §2–3. Four segments (logistics, air taxis, inspection, EMS) have different competitive logics. HHI is a screen on a defined market, not a city-wide LAE score. Sandbox counts are programme facts, not shares.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w02-q2" data-correct="c">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">2. The Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI) in Week 2 is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q2" value="a"> The sum of firms’ market shares (percent), used as a binding legal threshold in Cap. 448G.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q2" value="b"> Average total cost per flight when utilization rises.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q2" value="c"> HHI = Σ s<sub>i</sub><sup>2</sup> from market shares — a concentration <em>screen</em>, not proof of dominance or a Cap. 448G test.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q2" value="d"> The same identity as economies of scale from bigger vehicles.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Named formula <a href="formulas.qmd#w02-hhi">Formulas · Week 2 · HHI</a>; Study checklist 3; §4. Higher HHI means more uneven shares. It does not prove market power alone. ATC and density are separate tools (§§5–6).</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w02-q3" data-correct="a">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">3. Economies of density (Week 2) mean…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q3" value="a"> Spreading fixed route / site cost over more volume on the <em>same</em> corridor and sites — not the same thing as bigger vehicles.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q3" value="b"> Lower average cost mainly by flying larger vehicles (economies of scale).</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q3" value="c"> That scarce pads never affect Bertrand price wars.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q3" value="d"> That entering the first Regulatory Sandbox automatically creates density.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 2; Study checklist 5; §6; <a href="formulas.qmd#w02-density">Formulas · density</a>. Contrast with scale. Scarce pads can soften Bertrand wars (Study checklist 8; §9). Sandbox entry ≠ density proof.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w02-q4" data-correct="c">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">4. Which statement matches the Week 2 sandbox / corridor guards?</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q4" value="a"> First-batch “38 of 72” and Sandbox X’s “33 modules” are interchangeable market-share statistics.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q4" value="b"> Sandbox participation proves Hong Kong firms dominate the GBA market.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q4" value="c"> Keep <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>; cite 38 of 72 and Sandbox X 33 modules separately; policy / trial corridors are not day-to-day operating service.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w02-q4" value="d"> U-space rules in Hong Kong statute set the HHI screen.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Study checklist 10–11; §8 Absolute programme facts. Learning objective 5: complementary capabilities ≠ trial as proof of dominance. U-space ≠ Hong Kong law (standing course guard).</div>
  </fieldset>

</div>
```

## Week 3 — Unit cost, revenue, and breakeven {#week-03}

Full notes: [Week 3](week-03.qmd) · On-week Self-check: [Week 3 · Self-check](week-03.qmd#self-check) · 4 questions.

```{=html}
<div class="selfcheck" id="selfcheck-w03" data-week="03">
  <p class="selfcheck-intro">Four questions from Week 3 learning objectives, the Study checklist, and named formulas (CAPEX/OPEX, CASK, breakeven). Keep the <strong>Hong Kong premium</strong> as hypotheses to test; <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>.</p>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w03-q1" data-correct="b">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">1. On the Week 3 cost stack, the first discipline is to…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q1" value="a"> Jump straight to CASK before listing cost items.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q1" value="b"> Separate CAPEX, recurring fixed OPEX, and activity-related variable cost — and remember certification cash is not automatically CAPEX.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q1" value="c"> Treat all Hong Kong costs as a fixed universal multiplier over GBA peers.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q1" value="d"> Equate CASK with profit per passenger.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 1; Study checklist 1–2, 4; §§2–3. Hong Kong premium is a hypothesis, not a universal multiplier. CASK is cost per available seat-km offered — not proof of profit (<a href="formulas.qmd#w03-cask">Formulas · CASK</a>).</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w03-q2" data-correct="a">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">2. CASK (cost per available seat-kilometre) is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q2" value="a"> Operating cost ÷ (available seats × kilometres flown) — cost per seat-km <em>offered</em>, whether sold or empty.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q2" value="b"> Ticket revenue ÷ revenue passenger-kilometres only.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q2" value="c"> The Cap. 448G statutory charge per kilometre.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q2" value="d"> Identical to cost per mission-kilometre for cargo.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Study checklist 5–6; §4; <a href="formulas.qmd#w03-cask">Formulas · CASK</a>. Mission-km is a different unit for cargo / public service. CASK does not by itself prove commercial viability.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w03-q3" data-correct="a">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">3. Breakeven units in the Week 3 classroom identity are…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q3" value="a"> Fixed cost ÷ (revenue per unit − variable cost per unit), then confronted with physical capacity.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q3" value="b"> Always equal to Sandbox X module counts.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q3" value="c"> Maximising load factor alone, even if contribution falls.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q3" value="d"> CAPEX ÷ ticket price, ignoring variable cost.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 3; Study checklist 8–9; §7; <a href="formulas.qmd#w03-be">Formulas · Breakeven</a>. Maximising load factor alone can destroy contribution (revenue-per-flight identity). Results must confront capacity.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w03-q4" data-correct="b">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">4. Which revenue-model statement matches Week 3?</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q4" value="a"> Pay-per-use, subscription, availability-based, and complementary models all place usage risk on the same party.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q4" value="b"> Compare models on predictability and who bears usage risk — availability payments can flip a loss to a profit sketch, but are not free insurance.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q4" value="c"> Weather downtime has no channel into required activity.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w03-q4" value="d"> NASA UAM framing is a Hong Kong cost quote you may paste into CASK.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 4–5; Study checklist 7, 11–12; §§5, 8. Weather loss channels and hedge limitations are explicit. NASA / CAAC materials are comparators / readings, not HK cost quotes.</div>
  </fieldset>

</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="selfcheck" id="selfcheck-w04" data-week="04">
  <p class="selfcheck-intro">Four questions from Week 4 learning objectives, the Study checklist, and named formulas (funnel, GC, elasticity, Q<sub>served</sub>). Public acceptance is an <em>explicit</em> scenario factor — never an invisible haircut. <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>.</p>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w04-q1" data-correct="c">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">1. The Week 4 commercial question is best stated as…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q1" value="a"> “Can the aircraft fly?” alone.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q1" value="b"> Whether Sandbox X has more modules than the first Regulatory Sandbox.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q1" value="c"> Whether there are enough customers at a viable price — potential funnel demand vs served trips under capacity.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q1" value="d"> Whether Cap. 448G A2 height equals ~1,000 m policy language.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Study checklist 1, 4–5; Learning objective 1; §§1–4. Keep passenger-trips, flights, and seats distinct. Height-band guards belong to Weeks 1 / 7 / 8, not this demand question.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w04-q2" data-correct="d">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">2. Door-to-door generalized cost in Week 4 is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q2" value="a"> Fare only — access and wait time never reverse mode ranking.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q2" value="b"> Identical to Week 1 short-form GC with no door-to-door extension.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q2" value="c"> A Cap. 448G statutory tariff schedule.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q2" value="d"> GC = fare + VOT × door-to-door time + other monetized burdens — access/wait friction can reverse which mode looks cheaper.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 2; Study checklist 6; §5; <a href="formulas.qmd#w04-gc">Formulas · Week 4 · GC</a>. Week 1 short form is ticket + VOT × travel time; Week 4 stresses full door-to-door burdens.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w04-q3" data-correct="a">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">3. Own-price elasticity of demand (classroom) measures…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q3" value="a"> % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in own price — and helps judge when a discount raises vs lowers revenue.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q3" value="b"> Only cross-elasticity with ground modes.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q3" value="c"> The same thing as HHI.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q3" value="d"> A fixed universal public-acceptance multiplier of 0.7.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 3; Study checklist 7–8; §6; <a href="formulas.qmd#w04-ed">Formulas · E<sub>d</sub></a>. Acceptance must be an explicit, defended factor (Study checklist 9), not a hidden constant.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w04-q4" data-correct="b">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">4. Under a capacity shock, served quantity is…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q4" value="a"> Always equal to unconstrained demand Q<sub>d</sub>.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q4" value="b"> Q<sub>served</sub> = min{Q<sub>demand</sub>, Q<sub>capacity</sub>}, then linked to Week 3 breakeven / required activity.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q4" value="c"> Sandbox first-batch selection counts.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w04-q4" value="d"> NASA / AiRMOUR survey totals pasted as Hong Kong demand.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 5; Study checklist 10–12; §9; <a href="formulas.qmd#w04-qserved">Formulas · Q<sub>served</sub></a>. NASA / AiRMOUR / EASA are comparators, not HK demand quotes.</div>
  </fieldset>

</div>
```

```{=html}
  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w05-q2" data-correct="c">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">2. Generalized site cost in Week 5 includes…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w05-q2" value="a"> Land rent only — access time never matters.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w05-q2" value="b"> Only the Sandbox X application fee.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w05-q2" value="c"> Annualized infrastructure cost + annual OPEX + monetized access burden — cheap remote land can still destroy Week 4 mode share.</label></li>
```

```{=html}
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Study checklist 3–4, 6; <a href="formulas.qmd#w10-noise">Formulas · noise</a>. Separate appraisal carbon dials from any claimed CAD carbon tax. AiRMOUR is a closed EU research action — not an OEM brand (Study checklist 9).</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w10-q3" data-correct="d">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">3. Operational electricity emissions e<sub>op</sub> are…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q3" value="a"> Always zero for electric aircraft.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q3" value="b"> Identical to privacy-control cost C<sub>priv</sub>.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q3" value="c"> Sandbox X’s environmental score.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q3" value="d"> e<sub>op</sub> = E<sub>kWh</sub> × f<sub>grid</sub> — state units and boundary; life-cycle e<sub>FU</sub> adds vehicle, battery, infrastructure, operations, end-of-life over use U.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 3; Study checklist 7–8; <a href="formulas.qmd#w10-eop">Formulas · e<sub>op</sub></a> and <a href="formulas.qmd#w10-efu">e<sub>FU</sub></a>. Hold functional unit constant when comparing modes.</div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w10-q4" data-correct="b">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">4. Privacy-control cost C<sub>priv</sub> = F<sub>gov</sub> + q v + A…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q4" value="a"> Is optional to ignore for onboard cameras.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q4" value="b"> Appraises governance / assurance cost at different assurance levels using necessity and proportionality — then design measurable KPIs (measure, KPI, payer) without inventing a 60 dB rule.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q4" value="c"> Equals OHKF value added.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w10-q4" value="d"> Waives public-acceptance concerns for all use cases equally.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 4–5; Study checklist 5, 9–12; <a href="formulas.qmd#w10-priv">Formulas · C<sub>priv</sub></a>. Segment acceptance by use case; cite Action Plan / Sandbox X language only to the issuer.</div>
  </fieldset>

</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="selfcheck" id="selfcheck-w11" data-week="11">

Integrate weeks without inventing corridor capacity; <strong>Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X</strong>; separate AC-013, AC-017, and Policy Address Action Plan.</p>

      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q1" value="b"> Replace analysis with TAM-as-forecast slides.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q1" value="c"> Trace one assumption change through demand → capacity → cost → cash flow → legitimacy with consistent units and causal links.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q1" value="d"> Treat Sandbox X as a safety waiver.</label></li>
    </ul>
    <div class="selfcheck-explain" hidden>Learning objective 1–2; Study checklist 1; §§1–2. Weak-evidence habits (TAM-as-forecast, multi-haircut, hidden downside) are called out (Study checklist 9).</div>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w11-q2" data-correct="a">
    <legend class="selfcheck-stem">2. The operating viability test identities include…</legend>
    <ul class="selfcheck-options">
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q2" value="a"> D<sub>served</sub> = min{D, K} and Π<sub>op</sub> = (p − v) D<sub>served</sub> − F — recomputed under capacity shocks with fixed D.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q2" value="b"> D<sub>served</sub> always equals unconstrained TAM.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q2" value="c"> Π<sub>op</sub> equals OHKF HK$350bn.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q2" value="d"> Viability ignores non-financial decision criteria.</label></li>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w11-q3" data-correct="b">

      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q3" value="c"> OHKF value added, operator revenue, and social benefit are interchangeable.</label></li>

  <fieldset class="selfcheck-q" id="sc-w11-q4" data-correct="d">

      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q4" value="c"> Use multi-haircut demand as the only evidence.</label></li>
      <li><label><input type="radio" name="sc-w11-q4" value="d"> Answer decision-maker lenses, show sensitivity / downside, put one Week 10 externality into a cash-flow or capacity channel, and close with stop/expand (or reject) conditions.</label></li>
```
